negative_reviews.author: erin
negative_reviews.text: although the ramen was a big portion, it was blander than expected, and i received 1 piece of pak choi😢. the staff are very efficient and the food came out quickly, but i wouldn't say this would be my go-to ramen spot. perhaps the other menu items are better, which may mean this review is not representative, but i wouldn't spend more than £5 for the ramen.

negative_reviews.author: A10 Beats
negative_reviews.text: Probably the worst resteraunt in Manchester honestly. I waited (no joke) 20 minuets to be seated. Not once did someone come over to say anything to me. When I was seated. No apology. Nothing. It then took them 10+ minuets to come over and take a drinks order. Me and my partner decided to leave before we had even ordered drinks. The WORST most infuriating place in Manchester. AVOID at all costs.

negative_reviews.author: Hassan Al-Ghawi
negative_reviews.text: Average food. Ordered steak tataki ramen and it could use more flavor and spice. Sushi makis were average.

issues: Covers steady; spend per head dropped a lot on 5 GBP and free ramens; sales over target.
Delivery prep time up about 2 minutes on a very busy Tuesday.
Labour 20.18%; more staff rostered this week and next as the 5 GBP promotion is not cooling down.
Food cost 28%; more ramen stock needed.
Three reviews: slow service on a busy Wednesday (staffing increased since, no further complaints), a 3 star on a small pak choi portion, a 3 star on bland steak.
Jen leaves on the 24th; one sushi chef applicant trialled Sunday, Andre says experienced and trainable; Roxy and Jamie training on the bar.
Fusion B2B events coming up; Nottingham event to be attended by the site alone.
Region: all broth now arrives pre diluted, chefs no longer add water on site (consistency fix for bland or salty broth complaints; Ross memo).
Region: Deliveroo integrated delivery app on an iPad plus an extra order summary printer per packing station; Inka will set each site up in person once delivered.
Region: focus on service, food quality and speed to retain the new 5 GBP ramen and app customers; managers free to schedule FOH retraining.
Covers rose by 607 (16.37%) week on week but spend per head fell by £3.19 (16.85%), which the report puts down to the many £5 ramen and free ramen vouchers redeemed.
Sales were £2,184.58 (2.68%) lower week on week but £11,571.74 (17.14%) ahead of target.
Labour of 20.18% was under the 21% target, with 23.31% projected for this week as more staff are put on for the £5 ramen promotion, while food cost of 28.76% was well over the 23% target.
Tom and Adan are on holiday in the same week, which is why Roxy and Jamie are being trained on the bar.
The front door repair is waiting for parts and the sound system repair is waiting for an amplifier to arrive, both medium priority.
Inka put the food cost spike and lower SPH down to about £18,000 of free ramen promotions, and the team is upselling sides such as edamame (AM Updates 14/10).
Region: a level 8 Halloween ramen with a super spicy factory chilli paste is launching with a video; one bag per site, about a teaspoon per bowl (AM Updates 14/10).
Region: snooze out of stock items on both Deliverect and the POS, or the whole delivery order fails (AM Updates 14/10).
Region: wage revenue baseline is 21% with up to 2% leeway; drinks cost moves to management, food cost to head chefs, new OKRs due end of November (AM Updates 14/10).
Region: a temporary reserve stock buffer (about £300) was agreed for the English sites to stop stockouts (AM Updates 14/10).
